case.court: Supreme Court of the United States
case.limits: A narrower CFAA leaves breach of contract as the live claim. Terms of service still bind, they simply are not criminal.
case.holding: Exceeding authorised access under the CFAA means obtaining information from areas of a computer that are off limits, not using information you were entitled to obtain for a purpose the owner would dislike.

live_cases.name: Amazon.com Services, LLC v. Perplexity AI, Inc.
Amazon.com Services LLC v. Perplexity AI, Inc.

case.why_ai_cites_it: It closes the theory that violating a terms-of-service clause is a federal crime, and it is the Supreme Court backing behind the scraping practices that produced most large training corpora.

reading.body:
Van Buren v. United States (2021) established that violating a website's terms of service is not a federal crime under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, removing the most expansive legal threat against automated data collection at scale.

The Court drew a precise boundary: exceeding authorized access means entering parts of a computer system one has no permission to enter, not misusing data one was legitimately permitted to retrieve. That distinction matters for AI specifically because the scraping operations that assembled most large training corpora depended on public access to public pages. Under the broader reading the government argued for, any terms-of-service clause could have converted routine data collection into a federal offense, threatening the pipeline between public internet content and model training before a single GPU was provisioned.

What the holding does not do is eliminate legal exposure. The data notes explicitly that breach of contract remains a live claim, and terms of service still bind as a civil matter. The two Amazon v. Perplexity AI cases listed here represent exactly that surviving theory: the criminal door is closed, the contractual door is open. The data does not cover how courts have ruled in those downstream disputes, only that Van Buren is the precedent cited behind the defense posture in them.
